Norovirus Outbreak Disrupts Retail Operations Across Sweden

A norovirus outbreak has struck Sweden’s retail sector, causing widespread staff shortages and operational challenges at stores nationwide. Retailers are reporting significant impacts as hundreds of employees have called in sick, prompting temporary closures, reduced opening hours, and intensified cleaning protocols at affected sites.

The outbreak, which began surfacing last week in Stockholm and Gothenburg, has since spread to multiple locations, according to the Swedish Retail Federation (Svenska Detaljhandelsföreningen). “We are seeing up to 30% absenteeism in some stores, particularly in grocery and general merchandise outlets,” said federation spokesperson Karin Löfgren. “This is putting enormous strain on teams and managers, who are working hard to keep stores open and safe.”

Several leading chains, including Värdevaruhus and CityMat, have temporarily closed select branches to contain the spread and sanitize premises. “Our primary concern is the health of our staff and customers,” stated CityMat’s HR director Erik Nordin. “We are following health authorities’ guidance and have increased the frequency of cleaning in all stores, particularly in high-touch areas.”

Retail workers’ union representatives have raised concerns about staff welfare and workload. “Many members are working double shifts to cover for colleagues who are ill,” said Lina Karlsson, chair of Handelsanställdas Fackförbund. “We urge employers to prioritize employee safety and not pressure sick staff to return before they are fully recovered.”

The outbreak has also led to delays in restocking shelves and longer checkout times, as fewer employees are available to assist customers. Some stores report difficulties in maintaining normal stock levels, especially for cleaning products and staple foods.

Health authorities have advised retailers to reinforce hand hygiene and consider temporary closures where necessary. “This is an evolving situation, and we expect continued disruptions over the coming week,” said Löfgren. The Swedish Retail Federation is monitoring the outbreak closely and providing regular updates to its members.
